harvestNote: Main harvest Oct-Jan; washed lots ship from Feb, naturals a little later.
profile: Intensely floral and fruity: bergamot, peach, blueberry in naturals, jasmine and stone fruit in washed lots. Light, silky body with bright, clean, lingering sweetness.
notable: Hambela (METAD), Shakiso and Uraga are the celebrated sub-zones; Guji split from Sidama as its own origin name only in the 2010s.
brewTip: Very dense, small beans drain slowly and extract readily; grind slightly coarser than you think and brew hot (94-96C) to pull florals without muddiness.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Jan; fresh crop lands abroad Mar-Jun.
profile: Washed: tea-like, jasmine, lemon, bergamot, delicate and clean. Natural: blueberry, strawberry, winey, heavier and sweeter. The archetype of floral Ethiopian coffee.
notable: Gedeo zone washing stations (Gedeb, Kochere, Aricha, Idido) are the most famous named stations in the world; the Yirgacheffe name dates to the 1970s.
brewTip: Small, dense beans with lots of fines; a coarser grind and a gentle, steady pour stop the drawdown from stalling and keep the cup transparent.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Jan, highest Bensa farms picking into February.
profile: Bright citrus and florals with rounder stone fruit and red berry; naturals from Bensa are candy-sweet with blueberry and tropical notes. Fuller body than Yirgacheffe.
notable: Bensa district (Daye Bensa, Bombe, Shantawene) is the Sidama area most seen on bags; Sidamo was the historic export grade name.
brewTip: Behaves like other southern Ethiopians: dense, fines-heavy, slow drawdown; use a slightly coarser grind and avoid aggressive agitation late in the brew.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Jan.
profile: Softer than the south: balanced, sweet, spiced with mild citrus and florals, sometimes winey; medium body and gentle acidity.
notable: Western Ethiopian forest coffee zone, historically known for clean, tea-like washed coffees from the Limu Kossa and Gera areas.
brewTip: Slightly lower grown and less dense than Guji; medium-fine grind and 92-94C water suit it, and it tolerates a faster pour.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Jan; Agaro cooperatives ship Mar-May.
profile: Agaro washed lots are juicy and sweet: ripe peach, apricot, honey and florals with a rounded, syrupy body. Less citric and more tropical than the south.
notable: Cooperatives such as Duromina, Nano Challa and Biftu Gudina made Agaro famous; the Kaffa and Gesha forests nearby are coffee's genetic birthplace.
brewTip: Dense beans that like heat; brew at 94-96C with a slightly coarser grind, and expect a sweet, syrupy cup that forgives small ratio changes.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Jan, sun-dried on the farm.
profile: Rustic natural: blueberry, dark chocolate, winey and spicy with a heavy, almost chewy body and low acidity. Variable; the best are jammy, the worst earthy.
notable: Eastern dry-region garden coffee, traditionally sun-dried by smallholders; one of the oldest coffee trade names and the original 'mocha' flavour reference.
brewTip: Less dense and often uneven in roast; grind a touch finer, use 90-93C water and a slower pour to tame harsher notes and bring out the fruit.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; smaller fly crop May-Jul.
profile: The classic Kenyan cup: blackcurrant, tomato, grapefruit, intense winey acidity with a juicy, heavy body and dark sugar finish. Powerful and vivid.
notable: Factories (wet mills) owned by cooperative societies on the slopes of Mt Kenya and the Aberdares, sold through the Nairobi auction; home of AA/AB grading fame.
brewTip: Very dense, hard beans with high acidity; grind fine, brew hot (95-96C) and use a slightly longer ratio (1:16-17) to open the acidity into sweetness.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; fly crop May-Jul.
profile: Bright red fruit and blackcurrant with a rounder sweetness than Nyeri: plum, red grape, caramel and citrus, syrupy body and long finish.
notable: Southern slope of Mt Kenya; red volcanic soils and factories like Karimikui, Kii and Kabare have made it the most sought-after Kenyan county recently.
brewTip: Dense and acid-forward; fine grind, 94-96C and a gentle bloom. If it tastes sharp, lengthen the ratio or coarsen slightly rather than lowering temperature.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; fly crop May-Jul.
profile: Juicy and sweet with blackcurrant, red apple and brown sugar; slightly softer acidity and more chocolate than Nyeri, with a clean finish.
notable: Central Kenya county between Nyeri and Kiambu; its factories have been winning more attention as roasters look beyond the famous names.
brewTip: Treat like other Kenyans: fine grind, hot water, full-immersion bloom; a slightly shorter ratio (1:15) emphasises its sweetness.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; fly crop May-Jul.
profile: Blackcurrant and citrus with a softer, rounder body than Nyeri; cola, brown sugar and red fruit. Approachable Kenyan brightness.
notable: South-eastern slopes of Mt Kenya; a smaller producing county whose factories (Kibugu, Gakundu, Kathangariri) appear on specialty bags.
brewTip: Dense beans; fine grind and 94-96C. Drains a little faster than Nyeri lots so you can push agitation for more sweetness.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; fly crop May-Jul.
profile: Balanced Kenyan profile: blackcurrant and plum with milder acidity, more caramel and cocoa, medium-heavy body.
notable: Home of larger estates near Nairobi and of the Coffee Research Institute in Ruiru, where Ruiru 11 and Batian were bred.
brewTip: Slightly less acid-driven than northern counties; fine-medium grind and 94C water; it handles shorter ratios without turning sour.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Jan; some estates pick into Feb.
profile: Sweeter and gentler than Mt Kenya coffees: red berry, caramel, mild citrus with a rounded body; estates sometimes release naturals with winey berry fruit.
notable: Rift Valley growing area west of Nairobi, mostly larger estates on volcanic soils; a newer name in specialty Kenyan lots.
brewTip: High-grown and dense; fine grind and hot water as for other Kenyans, but its softer acidity tolerates 92-94C.

harvestNote: Single harvest Mar-Jun (Mar-Jul at highest sites); exports from Jul.
profile: Red apple, orange, black tea and caramel with silky body and crisp, clean acidity; naturals add strawberry and winey notes. Occasional potato defect.
notable: A washing-station revolution after 2002 (PEARL project) turned Rwanda into a specialty origin; Nyamasheke and Lake Kivu stations are most seen on bags.
brewTip: Dense Bourbon beans with uniform size; medium-fine grind, 93-95C. Extracts easily and cleanly, so it is a forgiving pour-over coffee.

harvestNote: Harvest Mar-Jul, peak Apr-Jun; new crop exports Aug-Oct.
profile: Bright and sweet: blackcurrant, cranberry, orange, honey and black tea with a juicy, medium body. Close cousin to Rwanda, often a little more floral.
notable: Kayanza and Ngozi provinces in the north hold the famous washing stations (Long Miles, Heza, Gaharo); ranked among Africa's best for price-quality.
brewTip: Dense, high-grown Bourbon; medium-fine grind and 93-95C. Blooms vigorously; a two-stage pour keeps acidity bright without harshness.

harvestNote: North (Kilimanjaro, Arusha) picks Jul-Dec; south (Mbeya, Mbinga) May-Oct.
profile: Bright, winey blackcurrant and citrus in the north, softer and sweeter with chocolate and plum in the south. Medium body; the famous peaberry grade is lively and clean.
notable: Kilimanjaro and Arusha estates in the north and Mbeya/Mbinga smallholders in the south; Tanzania Peaberry is the best-known export grade.
brewTip: Moderately dense; medium-fine grind at 93-94C. Northern lots behave like a gentler Kenya; southern lots suit slightly finer grinding.

harvestNote: Elgon main harvest Oct-Feb; Rwenzori main crop Apr-Jul with a second Oct-Dec.
profile: Full-bodied with cocoa, dried fruit and mild citrus; washed Elgon lots can be clean and sweet with red apple, naturals winey and heavy.
notable: Africa's largest coffee exporter (mostly Robusta); arabica from Mt Elgon (Sipi, Bugisu) and the Rwenzoris is the specialty face of the country.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind and 92-94C. Tends to extract quickly, so avoid very fine grinds that push bitterness into the heavy body.

harvestNote: Main harvest Mar-Jun (some stations into Jul); small secondary Sep-Dec.
profile: Rich and sweet: dark chocolate, plum, brown sugar and gentle citrus with a creamy body; the best are juicy with black tea and red fruit.
notable: Smallholder cooperatives (SOPACDI, Muungano, Kawa Kabuya) on the shores of Lake Kivu rebuilt the trade after conflict; Idjwi island lots are prized.
brewTip: Dense Bourbon; medium-fine grind, 93-94C. The heavier body rewards a slightly shorter ratio (1:15) and firm agitation during bloom.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Dec; mitaca (second crop) Apr-Jun. Fresh lots nearly year-round.
profile: Juicy and sweet: red apple, panela, orange, caramel with lively acidity and a round, creamy body. Pink Bourbon lots are floral and tropical.
notable: Colombia's largest and most awarded department, home to Pitalito, San Agustín, Acevedo and famous farms like El Paraíso, Monteblanco and El Diviso.
brewTip: Dense but even; medium-fine grind and 93-95C. Washed lots are forgiving; experimental ferments extract fast, so coarsen a little and shorten contact.

harvestNote: Single main harvest Apr-Aug, peaking Jun-Jul; exports from Aug.
profile: Among the brightest Colombians: lime, white grape, florals and sugary sweetness with a crisp, delicate body. Clean and intense.
notable: Extremely high, steep farms near the Ecuador border; Buesaco and La Unión won repeated Cup of Excellence top places for tiny smallholders.
brewTip: Very dense, small beans; grind fine and brew hot (95-96C). Slow drawdown is normal; slightly longer ratio (1:16-17) softens the acidity.

harvestNote: Two crops: Apr-Jun and Oct-Dec; south (Planadas) peaks May-Jun.
profile: Balanced and sweet: red fruit, milk chocolate, caramel, orange acidity with medium-full body; Planadas lots can be strikingly clean and floral.
notable: Planadas and Gaitania in the south, once off-limits during the conflict, now produce some of Colombia's most awarded smallholder lots.
brewTip: Dense; medium-fine grind and 93-94C. Tolerates stronger ratios well and rarely turns astringent.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Dec; mitaca Apr-Jun in many municipalities.
profile: Sweet and floral with citrus, caramel and panela; medium body and clean, bright acidity. Often slightly softer than Nariño, more aromatic than Huila.
notable: Holds a Protected Denomination of Origin; Inzá, Popayán plateau and El Tambo smallholders dominate specialty exports.
brewTip: Dense, high-grown; medium-fine grind and 94C. A longer bloom (45s) helps these tightly packed beans degas before pouring.

harvestNote: Main crop Oct-Dec; mitaca Apr-Jun.
profile: Classic 'Colombian' balance: milk chocolate, caramel, red apple, nutty sweetness with medium body and gentle acidity. Jardín and Urrao lots can be floral.
notable: The historic heart of Colombia's coffee culture around Medellín; the FNC's Medellín Excelso grade and Jardín's experimental producers are both from here.
brewTip: Medium-high density; medium grind and 92-94C. Forgiving and consistent, a good coffee for dialling in a new brewer.

harvestNote: Main harvest Oct-Jan; small mitaca Apr-May.
profile: Rounder and lower-acid than southern Colombia: milk chocolate, dried fruit, nuts, brown sugar with full body. Shade-grown lots are soft and sweet.
notable: Colombia's oldest coffee region near the Venezuelan border, known for shade-grown, often organic production; Hacienda El Roble pioneered variety gardens.
brewTip: Lower grown and softer; medium grind, 91-93C and a slightly shorter ratio keep the body rich without flatness.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep (dry season), often mechanised; new crop ships Aug-Nov.
profile: Nutty, chocolate, caramel and dried fruit with low acidity and a heavy, smooth body; naturals add raisin and winey notes. The classic espresso base.
notable: Flat plateau farms with Brazil's first Denomination of Origin for coffee; large, technified estates such as Daterra set the standard for consistency.
brewTip: Low-grown, soft beans that extract fast: grind coarser than for African coffees, use 90-93C, and a short ratio (1:14-15) to keep the body sweet, not bitter.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep; Mantiqueira hill farms pick into Sep-Oct.
profile: Sweet and rounded: milk chocolate, hazelnut, red apple and caramel with gentle citric acidity and creamy body; Mantiqueira Yellow Bourbons are floral and sugary.
notable: Brazil's largest arabica region; the Mantiqueira de Minas hills (Carmo de Minas) have won most Brazilian Cup of Excellence titles.
brewTip: Medium-low density; medium-coarse grind, 91-93C and a short, steady pour. Over-extraction shows quickly as bitterness, so keep contact time modest.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep.
profile: Full-bodied with chocolate, toffee, nuts and a soft fruit sweetness; low acidity, heavy and smooth. Reliable, comforting Brazilian cup.
notable: Named after the Mogiana railway on the São Paulo-Minas border; Alta Mogiana around Franca is the premium sub-zone with its own producer association.
brewTip: Soft beans; medium-coarse grind, 90-92C, short ratio. Great for bypass or stronger brews; avoid long drawdowns.

harvestNote: Harvest Jun-Sep, later than most of Brazil.
profile: Brighter than typical Brazil: red fruit, cocoa, honey and florals with a cleaner, lighter body thanks to altitude. Cup of Excellence winners show stone fruit.
notable: High plateau in Bahia's national park area where small farms around Piatã have repeatedly topped Brazil's Cup of Excellence.
brewTip: Denser than lowland Brazil; medium grind, 92-94C. Behaves closer to a Central American coffee than a Cerrado natural.

harvestNote: Arabica harvest May-Sep in the Caparaó mountains; Conilon lowlands pick Apr-Jul.
profile: Sweet and juicy mountain coffee: yellow fruit, cocoa, honey and gentle citrus with a medium body; cleaner and brighter than central Brazil.
notable: Caparaó, on the border with Minas, is a rising specialty zone of tiny hillside farms; the state is also Brazil's Robusta (Conilon) capital.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind, 92-93C. Naturals extract quickly, so a slightly coarser grind keeps the fruit clean.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep in the north (Cajamarca, Amazonas); Cusco and Puno slightly later, Jun-Oct.
profile: Sweet and balanced: milk chocolate, caramel, red apple and soft citrus with a silky, medium body; the best micro-lots are floral and juicy.
notable: Jaén and San Ignacio in Cajamarca are Peru's most awarded zones; cooperatives (Cenfrocafé, Sol y Café) and tiny farms dominate, mostly organic.
brewTip: Dense and clean; medium-fine grind and 93-94C. Very forgiving; it rarely turns astringent even at fine grinds.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep (peak Jun-Aug); some high farms pick into Oct.
profile: Elegant and sweet: milk chocolate, red fruit, mandarin and floral notes with silky body and crisp, clean acidity. Java and Gesha lots are intensely aromatic.
notable: Tiny production from the Yungas valleys; Agricafe's Sol de la Mañana programme and Caranavi's smallholders produce the country's celebrated micro-lots.
brewTip: High-grown and dense; medium-fine grind and 94C. Delicate florals fade with over-extraction, so keep contact time moderate.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Sep in the south; Pichincha (north) Jun-Oct.
profile: Refined and sweet: stone fruit, caramel, florals and citrus with bright acidity and silky body; Sidra and Typica Mejorado lots are perfumed and tropical.
notable: Southern highlands near Peru produce Ecuador's finest lots; small volume but prestigious farms (La Papaya, Finca Soledad) and new varieties like Sidra.
brewTip: High-grown and dense; medium-fine grind at 94C. Aromatic varieties reward a longer ratio and gentle pour to protect florals.

harvestNote: Late harvest Jan-Apr thanks to altitude and the dry Mexican winds.
profile: Bright, winey and sweet: red apple, orange, caramel, dried fruit with crisp acidity and medium-full body. Complex and elegant.
notable: Non-volcanic limestone highlands on the Mexican border; El Injerto and the La Libertad area have repeatedly won Guatemala's Cup of Excellence.
brewTip: Dense, hard beans; medium-fine grind and 94-95C. Extracts cleanly; it suits a slightly longer ratio (1:16) that lets acidity shine.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb.
profile: Rich and balanced: cocoa, caramel, orange, smoky spice with a full, velvety body and refined acidity. The classic Guatemalan estate cup.
notable: Volcanic valley between Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes; shade-grown estates with a protected 'Genuine Antigua' mark run by the producers' association.
brewTip: Dense volcanic beans; medium-fine grind and 93-94C. Body-forward, so it stays sweet at shorter ratios (1:15).

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, higher farms into Apr.
profile: Lively and sweet: red fruit, chocolate, honey, citrus with a juicy, medium body; higher and often brighter than neighbouring Antigua.
notable: Steep volcanic slopes west of Antigua, renewed by ash from Fuego; Finca La Soledad and the Pérez family's Gesha/Pacamara lots are the famous names.
brewTip: Dense; medium-fine grind, 94C. Blooms strongly; a longer bloom and two pours give a clean, bright cup.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb; highest farms pick into Apr.
profile: Clean and bright: orange, red apple, caramel and honey with crisp acidity and silky medium body. Honey process adds sugary, jammy sweetness.
notable: The Los Santos mountains are Costa Rica's most famous zone; micro-mill revolution of the 2000s and the 'honey process' were pioneered here.
brewTip: Very dense, hard beans; medium-fine grind and 94-95C. Honey lots drain slower than washed; coarsen slightly if the bed stalls.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Feb, peak Dec-Jan.
profile: Sweet and fruit-forward: peach, honey, vanilla, orange with medium body and bright but soft acidity; naturals and black honeys are jammy and winey.
notable: Home of the Villa Sarchí variety and a cluster of innovative micro-mills (Las Lajas, Helsar, Sumava, Cordillera de Fuego) that drive processing experiments.
brewTip: Dense; medium-fine grind and 93-94C. Processed lots can taste heavy if over-extracted; coarser grind and faster pour keep them clean.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Feb; Turrialba to the east starts earlier (Jul-Dec).
profile: Balanced and approachable: chocolate, honey, mild citrus and red fruit with medium body and gentle acidity.
notable: The oldest coffee zone in the country around the capital, with historic estates (Doka, La Minita) on the slopes of the Poás and Barva volcanoes.
brewTip: Moderately dense; medium grind and 92-94C. An easy, forgiving pour-over that suits standard 1:16 recipes.

harvestNote: Harvest Jan-Apr, later than lower Honduran zones; peak Feb-Mar.
profile: Juicy and complex: tropical fruit, mango, florals, brown sugar with vivid acidity and silky body; Pacas lots can taste surprisingly like an Ethiopian.
notable: Santa Bárbara mountain farms (Las Flores, El Cielito) around Lake Yojoa dominate Honduran Cup of Excellence; Marcala (La Paz) is the other famous zone.
brewTip: Dense; medium-fine grind and 94C. Fruity lots are delicate and sweeten with a longer ratio; avoid harsh agitation.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb.
profile: Rounded and chocolatey: cocoa, caramel, red apple, sweet spice with full body and soft acidity. Comfortable and sweet.
notable: Western Honduras near the Mayan ruins; cooperative Capucas and the Corquín area are well known. Honduras is Central America's largest producer.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind and 92-93C. Body-forward and forgiving; good for stronger ratios.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Feb; highest Chalatenango farms into Apr.
profile: Sweet and soft: honey, caramel, red apple, cocoa with a creamy body and mild acidity; Pacamara lots are big, juicy, floral and savoury.
notable: Birthplace of the Pacas and Pacamara varieties and a stronghold of old Bourbon; estates on the Santa Ana volcano win Cup of Excellence regularly.
brewTip: Medium-high density; medium grind, 92-94C. Pacamara's large beans need a slightly finer grind than their size suggests to extract evenly.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb.
profile: Mellow and sweet: milk chocolate, nuts, caramel, mild red fruit and soft acidity with a round body; Maracaturra and Java lots are brighter and floral.
notable: Jinotega and Matagalpa grow most of Nicaragua's coffee; Nueva Segovia (Dipilto, Mozonte) estates have taken most Cup of Excellence wins.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind and 92-93C. Low acidity means it can taste flat if under-extracted, so grind on the finer side of medium.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Apr; Gesha on the highest farms picks Feb-Apr.
profile: Panama Gesha is jasmine, bergamot, peach and tropical fruit with tea-like clarity and sparkling acidity; Catuaí lots are sweet, chocolatey and balanced.
notable: Hacienda La Esmeralda's 2004 Best of Panama lot launched the Gesha phenomenon; Elida, Lamastus and Finca Deborah set world auction records.
brewTip: Gesha is low-density and porous for its altitude: grind a bit coarser, brew 90-93C and use a longer ratio (1:16-17) so florals are not buried.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Apr, the highest farms (Finca Sophia, Nuvo) into May.
profile: Elegant and sweet: florals, stone fruit, honey and citrus with silky body; naturals are winey and tropical. Slightly fuller than Boquete at the same altitude.
notable: The western slope of Volcán Barú (Tierras Altas); Finca Hartmann's shade forests and Finca Sophia (one of the world's highest farms) are the landmarks.
brewTip: Treat like Boquete: coarser grind for Gesha, 91-94C, longer ratio; Catuaí and Pacamara lots handle standard 1:16 at 94C.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Feb; highest Sierra Madre farms into Apr.
profile: Balanced and sweet: milk chocolate, nuts, caramel, orange and soft red fruit with medium body and gentle acidity. Clean, easy-drinking.
notable: Mexico's largest producing state on the Guatemalan border; the Soconusco estates and El Triunfo reserve cooperatives (mostly organic) are the known names.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind, 92-93C. Forgiving and consistent; a good starting coffee for new brewers.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb.
profile: Delicate and sweet: honey, chocolate, red apple, florals and a soft, tea-like body with mild acidity; Pluma Hidalgo Typicas are prized for elegance.
notable: Pluma Hidalgo in the Sierra Sur has a denomination of origin for its Typica-based coffee; small indigenous farms and cooperatives such as CEPCO dominate.
brewTip: Medium-low density; medium grind and 91-93C. Delicate cups are easily over-extracted; keep contact time moderate and ratios around 1:16.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Feb; Pico de Orizaba foothills into Apr.
profile: Soft, sweet and clean: caramel, cocoa, orange, nuts and mild florals with a light-medium body. Higher farms near Pico de Orizaba are brighter.
notable: Mexico's oldest coffee zone around Coatepec and Huatusco; the Gulf-facing slopes are a hub for Mexican Cup of Excellence and specialty experimentation.
brewTip: Medium-low density; medium grind, 91-93C. Lighter-bodied, so a slightly shorter ratio (1:15) adds weight without bitterness.

harvestNote: Harvest Oct-Dec (some valleys Sep-Jan); sun-dried on rooftops, exports Jan-Apr.
profile: Wild, winey and spiced: dried fruit, dark chocolate, tobacco, cardamom and red wine with a heavy, syrupy body; modern lots are cleaner with berry and florals.
notable: The first place coffee was cultivated and traded (via the port of Mokha); terraced mountain gardens with unique 'Yemenia' genetics, exported by Qima, Mokha and others.
brewTip: Small, uneven, low-moisture beans that extract fast: grind coarser, brew 90-92C, and use a short ratio (1:14-15); over-extraction turns the spice harsh.

harvestNote: Gayo main harvest Sep-Dec, second crop Mar-May; Lintong peaks Oct-Jan with a fly crop around Jun.
profile: Wet-hulled: earthy, herbal, cedar, dark chocolate, tobacco with a heavy, syrupy body and low acidity. Fully washed Gayo lots are cleaner: spice, citrus, brown sugar.
notable: The Gayo highlands around Lake Tawar (Takengon) produce most of Indonesia's specialty arabica; wet-hulling (giling basah) gives the signature bluish-green beans.
brewTip: Wet-hulled beans are soft and extract fast: grind coarser, brew 88-92C and keep ratios short (1:14-15). Washed Gayo lots can take 93C and a finer grind.

harvestNote: Harvest Jun-Sep on the Ijen estates; West Java highlands pick May-Aug.
profile: Washed Java is clean, mellow and spicy: cocoa, cedar, nuts, mild citrus with a heavy, smooth body. West Java naturals are fruitier, with red berry and brown sugar.
notable: The Dutch colonial estates (Jampit, Blawan, Kayumas) on the Ijen plateau give the 'Java' name; West Java's Frinsa and Puntang farms lead the specialty revival.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind, 91-93C. Washed estate lots are forgiving; naturals extract fast, so coarsen slightly.

harvestNote: Harvest Jun-Sep, peak Jul-Aug.
profile: Deep and syrupy: dark chocolate, ripe fruit, spice, sweet tobacco and cedar with a heavy body and mild acidity; washed lots show caramel and citrus.
notable: Highland Tana Toraja villages (Sapan, Pulu-Pulu) and the Japanese-backed Toarco estate; Kalosi is the historic trading name for these coffees.
brewTip: Wet-hulled beans are soft: grind coarser, brew 89-92C and keep the ratio short; the body carries sweetness even with a quick drawdown.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Aug, peak Jun-Jul.
profile: Soft and sweet: milk chocolate, citrus, brown sugar and gentle florals with a medium, syrupy body; naturals are winey with tropical fruit.
notable: Grown on the slopes of Mount Batur by Subak Abian farmer groups, intercropped with oranges; Kintamani holds Indonesia's first coffee geographical indication.
brewTip: Medium density, often washed rather than wet-hulled; medium grind and 92-93C. Clean and forgiving, closer to a Central American in the cup.

harvestNote: Harvest May-Aug, peak Jun-Jul.
profile: Sweet and heavy: dark chocolate, tobacco, dried fruit, floral spice with a syrupy body and low acidity; cleaner than Sumatra with more fruit.
notable: Bajawa district farms on the volcanic slopes of Inerie; the Ngada and Manggarai regencies both hold Indonesian geographical indications.
brewTip: Soft, wet-hulled beans: coarser grind, 89-92C and a short ratio. Washed lots can be treated like a Bali coffee at 92-93C.

harvestNote: Harvest Apr-Sep, peak May-Jul; new crop ships Aug-Nov.
profile: Full and fruity: tropical fruit, red apple, brown sugar, herbal and nutty notes with a rich body and bright but rounded acidity. Some lots are wild and winey.
notable: Jamaica Blue Mountain seedlings planted in the 1920s; estates like Sigri and Kimel plus thousands of highland 'garden' smallholders in the Wahgi Valley.
brewTip: Dense, high-grown beans; medium-fine grind and 93-94C. Rustic lots benefit from a slightly coarser grind to keep ferment notes in check.

harvestNote: Arabica harvest Nov-Feb, peak Dec-Jan; Robusta Jan-Mar; monsooning Jun-Sep.
profile: Soft, spiced and sweet: cocoa, nuts, dried fruit, warm spice with a heavy body and low acidity; estate micro-lots add citrus and florals. Monsooned coffee is mellow and musty.
notable: Baba Budan planted India's first coffee here in the 1600s; shade-grown estates in the Western Ghats intercropped with pepper and cardamom.
brewTip: Medium-low density; medium grind, 91-93C and a short ratio (1:15). Monsooned beans are porous and need a coarse grind and cooler water.

harvestNote: Arabica harvest Nov-Feb, peak Dec-Jan; Son La (north) Oct-Jan.
profile: Clean, mild and sweet: chocolate, caramel, mild citrus and dried fruit with medium body and soft acidity; Typica lots from Cau Dat are more floral and tea-like.
notable: The cool Da Lat plateau is the heart of Vietnamese arabica in a country dominated by Robusta; K'Ho and Cau Dat farms lead the specialty movement.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind, 92-93C. Catimor lots can show vegetal notes if pushed, so avoid very fine grinds and long contact.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Feb.
profile: Soft and sweet: milk chocolate, nuts, caramel, mild citrus and red fruit with medium body and gentle acidity; naturals add berry and winey notes.
notable: Hill-tribe villages in the far north (Doi Chaang, Mae Jantai, Pha Hee) grew out of royal crop-substitution projects; Thai barista culture drives quality.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind and 92-93C. Catimor-heavy lots dislike over-extraction; keep the ratio around 1:15-16 and the grind medium.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Feb.
profile: Clean and mellow: milk chocolate, nuts, caramel, plum and mild citrus with medium body and soft acidity; experimental naturals are jammy and tropical.
notable: Nearly all Chinese coffee grows in Yunnan's Pu'er, Baoshan and Dehong prefectures; rapid quality growth since 2010 with washing stations and micro-lots.
brewTip: Medium density; medium grind, 92-93C. Catimor lots can taste vegetal if over-extracted, so stay at 1:15-16 and avoid very fine grinds.

harvestNote: Harvest Dec-Mar, peak Jan-Feb.
profile: Natural Ywangan lots are sweet and winey: strawberry, dried fruit, honey, cocoa with a juicy body and bright acidity; washed lots are clean with citrus and caramel.
notable: A community-based specialty programme since 2014 made Ywangan village naturals the face of Burmese coffee; Pyin Oo Lwin is the older estate zone.
brewTip: Medium-high density; medium grind and 92-94C. Naturals are forgiving but extract fast; coarsen slightly if the fruit turns boozy.

harvestNote: Harvest Nov-Mar, peak Dec-Jan.
profile: Delicate and sweet: stone fruit, florals, honey, brown sugar with a tea-like body and gentle acidity; the best lots echo a light-roast Panama in clarity.
notable: Tiny production of extremely expensive, meticulously processed micro-lots; Alishan tea-country farms (Zou Zhou Yuan, Zhuo Wu) win national and international awards.
brewTip: Medium density, very clean; medium grind and 92-94C. Use a longer ratio (1:16-17) and gentle pours to show the florals.

harvestNote: Harvest Aug-Jan, peak Sep-Nov; cherry ripens in several passes.
profile: Smooth, mild and sweet: milk chocolate, butter, brown sugar, mild citrus and nuts with a silky body and gentle acidity. Prized for softness, not intensity.
notable: A narrow belt of small farms on the Hualalai and Mauna Loa slopes; Hawaii's grading (Extra Fancy, Fancy, Peaberry) and the Kona name are state-protected.
brewTip: Low-grown, soft beans that extract quickly: grind medium-coarse, brew 90-92C and keep ratios short (1:14-15) so the delicate sweetness is not washed out.
